principles: Update tests to assert CURRENT correct behavior; never weaken or delete a safety assertion to make it green
Confirm production is intended/correct BEFORE touching a test; if a smoke reveals a real production bug, escalate not paper over
Change only test files; zero production code change (an edit to a non-test file means it is a real bug to escalate)
Each fixed smoke must pass standalone (node ...-smoke.js exit 0) with its original safety intent intact
drivers: The gate battery does not run these smokes, so per-smoke standalone verification is the only real evidence
The dominant risk is the inverse of a normal bug-fix: a careless make-it-green that masks a future real regression
Scope must stay bounded: P5 timeout/env family and B-6666 burndown are explicitly deferred

options.name: per-smoke-confirm-then-update
pros: Confirm correct current behavior against production + the changing story, then update the assertion/setup to match
Preserves safety intent; surfaces real bugs as escalations
Matches the documented allowlist mechanism for functional-CJK test fixtures
cons: Slower: each smoke needs root-cause reading not a blind regex bump

options.name: delete-or-relax-assertions
pros: Fast: delete or relax the failing assertions
cons: Hides behavior; could mask real regressions

options.name: revert-behavior-to-old-tests
cons: Requires reverting intended/correct behavior changes (scope-boundary gate, B-097f, B-72df); rejected

rationale: This approach is the only one that restores trust in the lifecycle/gate smokes without weakening them or touching production. The behavior changes the tests lag behind (scope-boundary INIT_CHECK gate, B-097f host-neutral prompts, B-72df scoped dirty-main DONE check, slug lowercasing, koala->lattice rename, message text drift) are all intended and correct; the tests are simply stale. delete-or-relax and revert-behavior both defeat the purpose. The survey already confirmed 14 STALE failures and 0 production bugs, but each implementer must re-confirm per smoke and escalate if a closer look reveals a genuine regression.

preMortem.scenario: An implementer weakens or deletes an assertion just to make a smoke pass
preMortem.trigger: A smoke is hard to root-cause and the implementer takes the shortcut of gutting the check
preMortem.consequence: A future real regression in that lifecycle/gate path goes undetected (worst possible outcome for a stabilization story)
preMortem.mitigation: Guardrail in every implementer prompt; require standalone-green WITH original safety intent intact; REVIEW test-coverage + quality reviewers specifically check no assertion was weakened/deleted; reviewer diff-reads each changed smoke

preMortem.scenario: A smoke that looks stale is actually a real production regression
preMortem.trigger: Production behavior genuinely changed wrongly, not intentionally, and the test was correct
preMortem.consequence: Updating the test to match the wrong behavior cements a real bug
preMortem.mitigation: Every implementer must read the production code + the story that changed it and CONFIRM intent before editing; if it is a real bug, STOP and escalate (open bug/separate story); the survey found 0 such cases but CHK-005 explicitly allows the escalate outcome

preMortem.scenario: An implementer edits a production (non-test) file to make a smoke pass
preMortem.trigger: The fix appears to require a production change (e.g. CJK in agent-prompt.ts)
preMortem.consequence: Violates strict scope and may mask the real issue
preMortem.mitigation: execution-boundary allowedPaths is restricted to the 15 *-smoke.ts files; any production edit is rejected and signals a real bug to escalate; CHK-004 CJK fix is confined to the test file usage-ledger-estimate-smoke.ts, with out-of-scope CJK resolved via the smoke allowlist not by touching production

preMortem.scenario: english-open-source-surface still fails after the in-scope CJK fix
preMortem.trigger: 4 other CJK sources (2 production, 2 functional-CJK test fixtures) remain beyond usage-ledger-estimate.ts
preMortem.consequence: CHK-004 userSees cannot be met within strict scope; risk of someone gutting the check or touching production to force it green
preMortem.mitigation: Resolve via the documented allowlist mechanism (functional-CJK test fixtures + pending-source-migration), confirmed as a scope-plan Open Question and resolved in writing; do NOT modify the check logic itself or touch production
